edges.evidence: The 2020 paper examines trust-building mechanisms in peer-to-peer accommodation from the providers' perspective, extending the earlier Airbnb trust study on how personal photos shape trust and reputation.
The Wuhan lockdown interview study extends the earlier China mental-health response commentary by providing detailed lived-experience evidence on how residents coped during the outbreak.
The 2020 paper on vocational workers narrows and applies the broader 2014 future-of-work agenda to a specific worker group facing automation and AI-related disruption.

The 2023 algorithmic management questionnaire paper addresses the measurement gap in worker experiences of algorithmic management, building on earlier empirical work that examined its effects on workplace well-being.
The 2025 review synthesizes the literature on algorithmic management and therefore builds on prior empirical evidence about how algorithmic management practices affect workplace well-being.

As a comprehensive review of algorithmic management, the 2025 paper builds on the 2023 scale-development study that introduced a questionnaire for measuring workers' experiences of algorithmic management.
The 2023 study extends prior scholarship on WhatsApp and private chat apps by applying it to food delivery workers' use of messaging groups for learning, resistance, and solidarity.

notes: Additional edges are concentrated in three clearer clusters: Airbnb/trust, COVID response in China, and algorithmic management/future-of-work; no strong contradiction pairs were identifiable from the supplied metadata, so none were added.
